title: 蝉（本以高难饱）
author: 李商隐
intro: A cicada high in a tree cries itself hoarse all night, and the tree does not care. Li Shangyin sees himself in it — an honest, poor official whose voice no one hears — and in the last line speaks to the insect as a fellow sufferer.
analysis: 古人以为蝉住在高树上，只喝露水，所以常用蝉比喻清高廉洁的人。这首诗前四句写蝉：它住得高，本来就难吃饱，叫得再辛苦也是白费力气；叫到五更天，声音稀稀落落快断了，可整棵树依旧碧绿，一点也不同情它。“一树碧无情”把树写得像冷漠的人，这是全诗最有名的一句。后四句转到自己：我官职低微，像水上漂着的树枝一样四处漂泊，家乡的田园早已长满荒草。最后说：麻烦你（蝉）用叫声来提醒我，我和你一样，全家清贫。前面写蝉，句句也是写人，这种手法叫“托物言志”——借写一样东西来表达自己的志向和处境。
analysisEn: People in ancient China believed the cicada lived high in the trees and drank nothing but dew, so it became a symbol of an honest person who stays pure and poor. The first four lines are about the insect. Living so high, it was never going to eat its fill, and all its crying is wasted effort. By the fifth watch, just before dawn, its voice is thin and breaking — yet the whole tree stays green and does not care in the least. “A whole tree of green, without feeling” turns the tree into a cold, indifferent person, and it is the poem’s most famous line. The second half turns to the poet. He is a low-ranking official drifting from post to post like a twig floating on water, and the fields at his old home are overgrown with weeds. In the last couplet he addresses the cicada directly: thank you for the warning your cry gives me — my whole family, like you, is “clean”, that is, honest and poor. Every line about the insect is also about the man. This way of writing — describing an object to express your own situation and values — is called 托物言志, “speaking one’s mind through a thing”.
background: Li Shangyin (c. 813–858) was one of the great late-Tang poets, known for dense, beautiful and often puzzling verse. Caught between two rival court factions, he spent his life in minor posts far from the capital; this poem is usually read as a picture of that frustrated career.
pronunciation: 五更 gēng；薄宦 bó huàn；梗 gěng；芜 wú；相警 xiāng jǐng。
version: 采用通行版本（如《唐诗三百首》所收），全诗完整。

lines.lit: Because it lives high, it is hard to eat its fill;
lines.en: Up so high, you were never going to eat your fill;

lines.lit: in vain it cries out its grievance, wasting its voice.
lines.en: all your aggrieved crying is wasted breath.

lines.lit: At the fifth watch, sparse, about to break off;
lines.en: Before dawn your voice thins and nearly fails,

lines.lit: a whole tree, green, without feeling.
lines.en: and the whole tree stays green, and does not care.

lines.lit: A petty official, like a twig still drifting;
lines.en: A minor official, I drift like a twig on the water;

lines.lit: my old home’s garden, the weeds have already levelled it.
lines.en: at home, the weeds have long since swallowed the garden.

lines.lit: I trouble you, sir, who warn me best;
lines.en: Thank you, cicada, for the warning in your cry —

lines.lit: I too, with my whole family, am clean and poor.
lines.en: like you, my whole household lives clean, and lives poor.

words.en: high (in the tree); also lofty, pure
words.note: 双关：蝉住在高处，也比喻人品清高。
今天仍常用，如“徒劳无功”。
这里是“含着怨恨”，比今天的“恨”更偏向委屈、不平。

words.en: the fifth watch — the last part of the night, before dawn
words.note: 古代把一夜分成五更，今天还说“三更半夜”。
这里指叫声稀疏；今天有“稀疏”“疏远”。
书面语，今天有“碧绿”“碧海蓝天”。
古语，“宦”是做官，今天有“宦官”“官宦人家”。

words.en: like a twig still drifting on water
words.note: “梗”是树枝，比喻漂泊不定；“泛”今天有“泛舟”。
书面语，今天还说“举家搬迁”。
这里指清贫、清白，今天有“清官”“两袖清风”。

imagery.name: 蝉
imagery.zh: 高处饮露、叫个不停却没人理的蝉，就是清廉、贫寒、怀才不遇的诗人自己。
imagery.en: The cicada — up high, living on dew, crying with no one listening — is the poet himself: honest, poor and overlooked.

imagery.name: 草
imagery.zh: “故园芜已平”，家乡的田园长满荒草，写出他漂泊在外、有家难回的凄凉。
imagery.en: Weeds have levelled the garden at his old home — a picture of how long he has been drifting, and how far he is from going back.
